summary:
Vatican City presents essentially no criminal-law exposure to a trans visitor. No documented criminal-law persecution of consensual homosexual conduct has occurred in the territory in modern times, and decriminalisation has nineteenth-century roots. Nothing about being trans is criminalised.

No legal recognition of gender exists in Vatican City. No anti-discrimination protection, facilities rule, or document-amendment mechanism covers a visitor or a resident.

Vatican City operates no prison system. It holds only a few cells for pre-trial detention, and anyone sentenced to imprisonment by Vatican City serves the term in Italian prisons at Vatican expense. Because no domestic prison system exists, there is no trans-specific prisoner-placement policy and no documented trans-prisoner placement case for this jurisdiction.

The Holy See's institutional posture against homosexuality and gender theory drives policy even where the city-state's own law imposes nothing. The Congregation for Catholic Education's 2019 document, Male and Female He Created Them, opposes what it calls gender theory, stating that it "denies the difference and reciprocity in nature of a man and a woman" and "eliminates the anthropological basis of the family." The legal baseline for a visitor is the city-state's own law, which is distinct from the Church's diplomatic and doctrinal positions.
tangentialFactors:
In 2008 Catholic officials rejected France's first-choice candidate as ambassador to the Holy See because he is gay, forcing Paris to name a different envoy. It is a documented instance of the Vatican government refusing an LGBT person in diplomatic relations, and it indicates the institutional climate a visibly LGBT person may encounter around the Holy See's own organs rather than any rule applied to visitors.

The current Holy See posture on blessing same-sex couples is set by the DDF declaration Fiducia Supplicans, issued under Pope Francis on 20 March 2023, which permits spontaneous blessings for same-sex couples while forbidding any rite resembling marriage. A January 2024 DDF press release reiterated that blessings never extend to the unions themselves.

Both items concern sexual orientation and institutional diplomacy more directly than they concern trans visitors, but they establish the direction of official policy in a territory where doctrine and government are held by the same institution.
localsOnly:
Residents of Vatican City have no mechanism to amend gender markers on identity documents, no route to legal recognition of gender, and no anti-discrimination remedy on grounds of gender identity or sexual orientation. The territory's small resident population stands under a civil code that contains no such provisions.

The 2019 Congregation for Catholic Education document is the reference point for education policy across the institutions the Holy See directs, framing gender identity as a question of anthropology to be corrected through dialogue rather than a matter of individual status.

Residents sentenced by Vatican City courts serve their sentences in Italian prisons, with the costs covered by Vatican City, because the territory has no prison of its own. Any resident serving a custodial sentence therefore leaves the jurisdiction's custody entirely, and no Vatican authority operates a placement policy inside the receiving facilities.
outOfScopeNotes:
No separate United States State Department Holy See chapter for 2023 or 2024 was available for this record; parts of the assessment rest on last-resort encyclopedic sources, and the historical and prison-capacity claims are not corroborated by a primary government travel advisory.

No source in the inventory addresses gender markers on passports or identity documents, border or entry screening, restroom access, or access to gender-affirming care for a visitor. Whether any of these are governed by Italian practice at the point of entry is unresolved rather than established here.

No documented trans-specific prisoner placement case was found for this jurisdiction. The absence of documentation is not evidence that a policy exists or that none does; it is unresolved.

The 2008 diplomatic rejection is reported by a single outlet in the inventory and was not independently corroborated within this pass.
